title: The more options you give, the less people buy

images.prompt: Ultra-detailed cinematic composite, 3:4 vertical. A glowing blue line graph hangs suspended in absolute black void, filling the upper two thirds of the frame: the y-axis reads MONEY, the x-axis reads CHOICES, rendered as thin luminous blue tick lines. Two points are marked on the x-axis, labelled 6 and 24. Rising from the point marked 6, a tall neat tower of stacked banknotes reaches high into the frame, crisp and voluminous. Rising from the point marked 24, only two lone banknotes and a small scatter of coins sit barely above the axis line, dwarfed by comparison. In the upper right, a circular inset cut-out shows an extreme macro close-up of the two lone banknotes and coins at point 24, rendered sharper and brighter than the main scene. One hard directional key light from the upper left, plus the blue graph line itself glowing as a cool practical light source — the one deliberate exception to the usual warm amber rule, because this image is a chart, not a scene. Tiny illegible technical annotation text in the top-left corner, like a lab dossier, thin tick marks along the right edge. Restricted palette: near-black void plus cool electric blue plus the muted green-grey of banknotes. High contrast, deep blacks, fine film grain, hyper-detailed macro photography look. Two dozen small jam jars sit in neat rows, filling the upper two thirds of the frame, labels turned away from camera, lids off, small tasting spoons beside each. A single warm amber deli lamp overhead is the practical light source, pooling warm light across the jars while the surrounding store falls into soft shadow.
